description:
Evaluate whether the process for merging PRs that touch soundness paths is proportionate to the risk it controls, and whether it works for agent-assisted delivery.

Current ceremony (since the oracle cut-over, #2758, 2026-10-09): a PR touching any path in .github/soundness-paths.txt needs the required `oracle-review` check to pass. That needs a success review of the current head from the `benchbox-oracle` App, or the human stand-in `Stand-in oracle review: APPROVE <sha>` posted after the oracle's latest review, with every oracle thread resolved. `make pr-arm` (scripts/pr_arm.py) arms such a PR and relies on that required check. The `Soundness review:` PR-body section this item was first written against is gone. The older landing helper scripts/pr_landing.py still refuses soundness PRs; that is tracked in pr-landing-soundness-refusal-unreachable-20261009 and is not part of this review.

Original observation (2026-10-01): in a backlog of 14 open non-draft develop PRs, 12 touched soundness paths. The surface reaches beyond equivalence and expected-results code: .github/workflows/ci.yml, publication/ledger-seed.json, scripts/publication/verify_lane_isolation.py, the explorer pipeline under _project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/, scripts/generate_corpus_inventory.py, and comment-only edits to an equivalence builder. The cut-over added the oracle's own policy file and reviewer package to the surface.

Questions to answer:
- Is the path set too broad? Which entries guard comparator or oracle correctness, and which only reflect that the file is sensitive (CI wiring, data seeds, publication tooling)? Should purely generated-data, comment-only, or docs-only changes be classified differently, given that every soundness PR now costs at least one model review?
- Is the oracle's cost per PR proportionate for low-risk entries? Count the cost per PR as reviewer runs, follow-up rounds, manual reruns of stale failing oracle-review runs, refusals, and stand-ins.
- Is drain reporting (soundness drain digest, green-unmerged sweep) enough to keep reviewed PRs from stalling?

Answered by the cut-over: the required review is bound to the head SHA and to the App's Bot identity.

Cost data needs about two weeks of use after the cut-over, so the review starts on 2026-10-23.

Output: a short written recommendation per question, and either follow-up items for approved changes or a decision to keep the ceremony as is, with the reason.
